results.query: In the cross-sectional pilot study of veterans, what cardiac MRI findings in people living with HIV suggested myocardial fibrosis and subclinical dysfunction?
results.answer: In the cross-sectional pilot study of veterans, higher growth differentiation factor (GDF)-15 blood levels were found among patients with HIV [PMID:41791688]. Increased extracellular volume on cardiac MRI was observed in people living with HIV, suggesting the presence of increased myocardial fibrosis [PMID:41791688]. Lower right heart function on MRI was found among patients with HIV, suggesting subclinical myocardial dysfunction in this population [PMID:41791688].

results.query: In the single-arm DYNAMITE study, what structural changes were measured at 9 months and what major adverse cardiac events were observed by 24 months after DynamX implantation?
results.answer: In the single-arm DYNAMITE study, structural changes measured at 9 months included an increase in mean device area from 8.15 ± 0.64 mm² to 8.53 ± 1.71 mm² and a decrease in mean in-device lumen area from 8.27 ± 1.78 mm² to 7.57 ± 1.86 mm² [PMID:41765253]. By 24 months after DynamX implantation in the DYNAMITE study, 4 patients (7.4%) experienced major adverse cardiac events, which included one target vessel myocardial infarction and four target lesion revascularization events [PMID:41765253].

results.query: What evidence did the small HIV pilot provide for myocardial fibrosis and right-ventricular dysfunction, and what longitudinal question remains unanswered?
results.answer: The small HIV pilot study found higher growth differentiation factor (GDF)-15 blood levels, increased extracellular volume, and lower right heart function on MRI among patients with HIV [PMID:41791688]. These findings suggest the presence of increased myocardial fibrosis and subclinical myocardial dysfunction in people living with HIV [PMID:41791688]. Limited data from this pilot study suggest that HIV may be associated with increased cardiac fibrosis and decreased right ventricular function [PMID:41791688]. This study highlights the need for larger longitudinal studies to better understand the trajectory of HIV-associated cardiac changes [PMID:41791688].

results.query: How was SCAR-Net built and validated for distinguishing postoperative breast scars from recurrent lesions, and how much did it change radiologist performance?
results.answer: SCAR-Net was developed using a dataset of 34,376 ultrasound images from 5,710 patients across four hospitals and incorporates scar-recurrence feature enhancer and boundary-sensitive attention network modules [PMID:42023157]. In multicenter validation, SCAR-Net significantly improved radiologists' diagnostic performance by increasing AUC from 0.810-0.824 to 0.939-0.942 [PMID:42023157]. The model increased sensitivity from 0.775-0.782 to 0.934-0.941 and specificity from 0.839-0.872 to 0.935-0.950 [PMID:42023157]. SCAR-Net demonstrated superior segmentation accuracy with Dice coefficients of 0.918-0.925 compared to traditional methods which had coefficients of 0.795-0.811 [PMID:42023157].

results.query: What target-specific tumor-localization evidence was reported for the LGR5 tracer [68Ga]Ga-LTP-02 and for the Nectin4 probes in their respective preclinical models?
results.answer: Dynamic PET imaging revealed that [68Ga]Ga-LTP-02 exhibited considerably higher uptake in LGR5-positive A549 xenografts (4.74 ± 0.44 %ID/mL) than in LGR5-negative NCI-H1299 xenografts (0.98 ± 0.08 %ID/mL) [PMID:42000453]. Biodistribution studies confirmed that [68Ga]Ga-LTP-02 can specifically target LGR5-positive tumors [PMID:42000453]. Cellular uptake assays demonstrated markedly higher accumulation of Nectin4-targeted tracers in MC38-Nectin4 cells compared with MC38 cells [PMID:41916034]. Biodistribution studies and PET imaging revealed pronounced and specific tracer accumulation in MC38-Nectin4 tumor models, whereas uptake in MC38 tumors remained substantially lower [PMID:41916034]. The tumor-to-muscle ratio for Nectin4 probes increased progressively over time and reached its maximum at 120 min post-injection [PMID:41916034]. Both Nectin4-targeted tracers exhibited increased hepatic uptake accompanied by reduced renal accumulation, indicating a shift toward enhanced hepatobiliary clearance [PMID:41916034].

results.query: How did AI assistance change diagnostic performance in the simulated prostate-MRI triage workflow and in multicenter breast-ultrasound scar-versus-recurrence assessment?
results.answer: In a meta-analysis of AI assistance across various studies, the pooled sensitivity increased to 0.79 (95% CI 0.71-0.88) and specificity to 0.87 (95% CI 0.82-0.91), though the overall difference in accuracy between clinicians with and without AI assistance was not statistically significant [PMC:doc260]. In a simulated prostate-MRI triaging workflow, an AI-driven pathway maintained comparable sensitivity (89.0%) while improving specificity by 11.5% to 69.2% compared to the conventional workflow [PMID:41960994].

results.query: What discrimination, sensitivity, and specificity did the catheter-related-thrombosis nomogram report in the oncology cohort?
results.answer: The catheter-related-thrombosis nomogram reported a discrimination area under the curve of 0.866, a sensitivity of 70.33%, and a specificity of 85.89% in the oncology cohort [PMID:42077124].

results.query: What sensitivity-specificity tradeoff did simulated prostate-MRI AI triage show, and what real-world clinical effect remains untested?
results.answer: The simulated AI-driven triaging workflow for prostate MRI maintained comparable sensitivity of 89.0% while improving specificity by 11.5% to reach 69.2% compared to the conventional radiologist workflow [PMID:41960994]. The AI system triaged and diagnosed examinations with a sensitivity of 94.7% and specificity of 94.7% in the simulated study [PMID:41960994]. Sensitivity and specificity measures vary with given thresholds, and future studies should provide more details on a reported threshold to clarify integration with MRI-based pathways [PMC:doc260].

results.query: Does the supplied prostate-MRI study establish that deploying AI triage reduces unnecessary biopsies or improves patient outcomes versus a radiologist-only workflow?
results.answer: A simulation study of an AI-driven triaging workflow demonstrated that the AI system improved simulated diagnostic workflow efficiency without compromising diagnostic accuracy for clinically significant prostate cancer [PMID:41960994]. In the simulation study, the AI-driven pathway maintained comparable sensitivity to radiologists but improved specificity by 11.5% [PMID:41960994]. The AI system triaged and diagnosed examinations with a sensitivity of 94.7% and a specificity of 94.7% in the simulation study [PMID:41960994]. Multimodal models that integrate imaging, clinical, and molecular data are stated to outperform traditional PSA-based strategies and reduce unnecessary biopsies [PMID:41969325]. A prospective bicenter study by Lee et al. demonstrated that incorporating a deep learning algorithm into the radiological workflow improved per-participant specificity while preserving comparable sensitivity [PMC:doc289].

results.query: How did the fMRI acceleration method and the MR anisotropic-diffusion filters address different image-reconstruction problems, and what validation result did each report?
results.answer: Algorithms combining modern diffusion models with classical techniques like compressed sensing generally report improved image quality at higher acceleration factors and improved robustness to domain shift [PMC:doc232]. For breast MRI, a study by Okolie et al showed that at an acceleration factor of 2, diffusion models produce images almost indistinguishable from the original in 99% of cases as rated by radiologists [PMC:doc232]. A study investigating a spatio-temporal diffusion-based reconstruction for cardiac imaging found that quantitative image metrics indicated superior image quality compared to baseline methods including compressed sensing-based techniques [PMID:41708490]. In the same cardiac study, expert reader scores implied consistent sharpness and reduced apparent noise for the proposed diffusion model compared to baseline methods [PMID:41708490]. Including temporal information within a diffusion model improved consistency between frames, reduced noise, and preserved sharpness in reconstructions of undersampled spiral acquisitions [PMID:41708490].

results.query: For surveillance of local nasopharyngeal carcinoma recurrence, what sensitivities were reported for nasopharyngeal-brush versus plasma EBV DNA testing?
results.answer: Nasopharyngeal brush EBV DNA detection demonstrated a sensitivity of 95.7% for detecting local recurrence of nasopharyngeal carcinoma [PMID:41631491]. Plasma EBV DNA testing demonstrated a sensitivity of 61.4% for detecting local recurrence of nasopharyngeal carcinoma [PMID:41631491].

results.query: What association did the hemodialysis study find between AV-access flow and LV mass, and why can it not establish that lowering access flow will improve cardiac outcomes?
results.answer: Higher AV access flow (brachial artery flow volume) was significantly associated with increased left ventricular mass index in hemodialysis patients [PMID:41644509]. The study found no statistically significant interaction between AV access flow and dialysis vintage regarding their effects on left ventricular mass index [PMID:41644509]. Because the study was a cross-sectional design, it cannot establish that lowering access flow will improve cardiac outcomes [PMID:41644509].

results.query: In the retrospective vacuum-assisted-birth cohort, which factors were independently associated with assisted vaginal birth, and how did mid/low-pelvic applications differ from perineal applications?
results.answer: In the retrospective vacuum-assisted-birth cohort, maternal age, mode of conception, epidural analgesia, gestational age, and newborn male sex were positively associated with assisted vaginal birth [PMID:42036403]. In the same cohort, parity was inversely associated with assisted vaginal birth [PMID:42036403]. Compared to perineal applications, mid/low pelvic vacuum applications were associated with greater blood loss [PMID:42036403]. Mid/low pelvic vacuum applications showed a higher episiotomy rate (95.5%) compared to perineal applications (88.2%) [PMID:42036403]. Ultrasound use was significantly increased in mid/low pelvic vacuum applications (62.4%) compared to perineal applications (23.5%) [PMID:42036403].

results.query: In the prospective thoracic ASRT study, what did online adaptation change in target coverage and organ-at-risk dose, and what treatment-time and toxicity results were reported?
results.answer: In the prospective thoracic ASRT study, online adaptation significantly improved target coverage with a median V100% change of +0.1%±2.5% compared to predicted plans (-2.6%±7.3%, p < 0.001) [PMID:42058324]. Online adaptation in the prospective thoracic ASRT study did not result in significant differences in organ-at-risk doses [PMID:42058324]. The median total treatment time for the ASRT workflow was 28 minutes, with an average 5-minute ASRT workflow [PMID:42058324]. No grade ≥ 3 toxicities were reported in the prospective thoracic ASRT study, while grade 2 events occurred in 10.3% of patients [PMID:42058324].

results.query: Does the supplied ASRT study show that adaptive skin radiotherapy improves local control or survival compared with nonadaptive thoracic radiotherapy?
results.answer: In a prospective study of lung patients treated with Adaptive Skin Radiotherapy (ASRT), the median total treatment time was 28 minutes with an average 5-minute ASRT workflow [PMID:42058324]. At a median follow-up of 19.8 months, the 1-year local control for the whole cohort treated with ASRT was 94% [PMID:42058324]. The study reported that no grade ≥3 toxicities were observed in patients treated with Adaptive Skin Radiotherapy (ASRT) [PMID:42058324]. Online adaptation using ASRT significantly improved target coverage compared to predicted plans without significant differences in organ-at-risk doses [PMID:42058324].
